messages:
Eve: Dropping a compact-row idea — show total tokens inline, expand chevron loads breakdown lazily. Quick mock: https://img.redwood/mock/compact-row-v2.png
Marcus: Nice. Two asks: keep download button visible per-row, and make sure the expand control is big enough on mobile.
Leah: Export caveat: current CSV assumes a flat list. If we lazy-load client-side, exports must use server param `expand=true` to include breakdowns. Otherwise exports will be missing rows.
Devin: Accessibility: chevron must be a <button> with aria-expanded and aria-controls. When breakdown finishes loading announce via `aria-live="polite"` so screen readers know counts updated.
Eve: Agreed. Also proposing a microcopy change: inline summary reads "2,450 tokens · details" instead of just a number so it reads like an affordance.
Marcus: Implementation note: render breakdown only on first expand and cache it. Avoid re-fetching on repeated opens. Add `data-invoice-id` to the rendered fragment for exports mapping.
Leah: For CSV shape, include `units_type` column and when `expand=true` emit extra rows with `line_item_id, project_id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens`. Document it in the API changelog.
Devin: Keyboard: Enter/Space to toggle, Tab to land on the expansion region, and when opened focus the first interactive element inside. Add a skip link for screen readers: "Skip to invoice details".
ux-bot: A11y checklist: contrast >=4.5 for chevron, visible focus ring, aria-live announcements, tooltip accessible by keyboard, avoid color-only states.
Eve: Acceptance criteria for PR: compact row on org list, visible per-row download, lazy-load expansion with caching, server-side `expand=true` for exports, aria attributes + aria-live, microcopy update, docs for CSV columns.
Marcus: Dev estimate: frontend 2 dev days, export API + docs 1-2 days, QA + a11y pass 1 day. I'll pick up export work, @eve takes frontend, @devin a11y review.
Leah: I'll loop in finance for CSV column names and run a quick compatibility test with their ingestion.
Eve: Thanks team — will post updated mock and a short prototype of keyboard flow in ~24h. :rocket:
